subject: Correlating Latent Factors between MIRT and Lavaan Package

messages.author: ac3350bb82db2fde
messages.subject: Correlating Latent Factors between MIRT and Lavaan Package
parts:
Dear Phil, 

Is it possible to correlate the latent factors extracted using the mirt() and those from the sem()?

I am using the same dataset, but with different packages (MIRT package and Lavaan package) to derived the same 4 latent factor results.  I am aware that the mirt() will allow within-item dimensionality, something which the sem() does not do. Therefore, I am interested to see how similar or different the latent factors are based on the different technique employed by using simple correlation. I would imagine there is some way to extract the latent factors, but I am not sure how to go about doing it.  Guidance here would be greatly appreciated. 


exmod1 <- mirt(SJT2, 4, rotate = 'oblimin',itemtype='gpcm', method="MHRM", SE=T)
summary(exmod1)

model3r <-   "Relationship_Building =~ RB1bScored + RB1cScored + RB1dScored + RB2aScored + RB2cScored + RB2dScored + RB3aScored + RB3bScored +   RB4dScored;
Achieving_Results  =~  AR1aScored +  AR2bScored + AR2cScored +AR2dScored + AR3bScored + AR3cScored + AR4aScored + AR4bScored + AR4cScored;
Analytical_Thinking = ~  AT2aScored + AT2cScored + AT3aScored +  AT4aScored + AT4bScored + AT4cScored ;
Planning_Organising =~ PO1cScored +  PO2bScored + PO2cScored + PO2dScored + PO3aScored + PO4aScored"

modelcfa3r <- sem(model=model3r, orthogonal=F, std.lv=T, data=SJT2)
summary(modelcfa3r, standardized=T, modindices = F, fit.measures=T)

Kind regards,
Aiden

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Correlating Latent Factors between MIRT and Lavaan Package
parts:
Hi Aiden,

I would say this isn't directly possible between the two packages for various reasons, the first being that you are trying to compare an exploratory IFA model with a confirmatory one via lavaan. It is much more consistent to either a) make a similar confirmatory pattern with the mirt.model() function (and telling lavaan that you have ordinal categorical variables with the ordered= argument), or b) create an exploratory factor analysis using a polychoric correlation matrix using something like the psych package.

I'm also not exactly sure what you mean by 'correlating the factors'. Latent variable modelling package don't usually store the latent estimates since they are random effects, and instead they have to be estimated using other methods like mirt::fscores() and lavaan::predict(). If you choose to model both as exploratory IFA models then rotation will be an issue for you, whereas confirmatory models don't suffer this complication and will give you more comparable factor scores. Hope that helps.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Correlating Latent Factors between MIRT and Lavaan Package
parts:
Hi Phil, 

It is possible to compare the AIC/BIC between the MIRT package and the lavaan package? If I were to treat the variables as categorial, the lavaan package will not produce the AIC/BIC because it uses the WLS estimator. However, If I treat the variables as continuous, that is possible because it uses the ML estimator. So I was wondering whether it is safe to assume that the model with the lower AIC/BIC is the better model regardless of the package used?

Thank you, 
Aiden

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Correlating Latent Factors between MIRT and Lavaan Package
parts:
In principle I suppose this is possible, but deliberately assuming the incorrect error structure by treating the data are continuous seems like a wrong approach and will produce large degrees of parameter bias. Besides, this is comparing a model that is clearly wrong versus one that is more plausible, which is why you should be sticking with the WLSMV estimator on a polychoric matrix in lavaan to better level the playing field. 

Phil
